Funnels rarely fail because of a bad idea. They fail because nobody owns the boring parts.

I run operations at Tantra. For every stage of a client's funnel I set three things:

→ One number we check every week

That's how a webinar keeps running instead of happening once. One client ran 11 webinars from May 2025 to February 2026, with a weekly analytics sheet and a 12-item experiment log behind them.

If you run operations, you know the real problem: work that depends on someone remembering.

Most B2B stacks leak at the joins. The lead isn't lost inside a tool. It's lost between two of them, and nobody notices until a sales rep asks why the CRM record is empty.

I'm the CTO at Tantra. I build the layer that connects it all:

→ Every form, booking and webinar event posts to one CRM
→ Every link is tagged by source, so you know which channel produced the call
→ AI agents send the invites, reminders and follow-ups from your own Gmail, LinkedIn and WhatsApp

One record per person, from first invite to signed client. That's the whole idea.
